clue.text: Niggardly priest promises to pay one mark to enter

indicators.note: the one-and-mark pair goes into the priest, so these words say one piece enters another

parts.note: a parson is a parish priest
I is the Roman numeral for one
M is a common abbreviation for mark, the old German currency
IOUs are written promises to pay a debt

explanation.surface: A stingy cleric offers IOUs and grudgingly hands over a single mark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Niggardly' is an old word for stingy; 'to enter' sets the IM pair inside the cleric's title.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone extremely mean with money, a straight synonym pair.

clue.text: Walked about inside with a disapproving look

indicators.note: inside places the word for about within the word for walked

parts.note: paced means walked steadily
of can mean about, as in 'speak of'

explanation.surface: Someone strolls around a room wearing a sour expression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like a container signal but gives OF (as in 'think of'); 'inside' is the real container word.
explanation.definitionFit: A prim, humourless face shows prudish displeasure.

clue.text: It's highly convenient for the rest of the birds

definitions.text: It's highly convenient for the rest of the birds

parts.words: It's highly convenient for the rest of the birds
parts.note: a perch set high up is a handy place for birds to sleep, rest meaning repose, not the remainder

explanation.definitionFit: A perch or place where birds settle to sleep at night.

clue.text: Unrehearsed concert I am put out about

indicators.note: about shows the scrambled letters go around the concert

parts.note: I'm is the contraction of I am

indicators.note: out signals the letters of I'm and put are scrambled

parts.note: a prom is a promenade concert, like the BBC Proms

explanation.surface: A performer upset by a hastily arranged gig.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges the letters to IMPTU; 'about' wraps them round the concert. The Proms are a famous London concert season.
explanation.definitionFit: Done on the spur of the moment, without preparation, is improvised.

clue.text: Honour surrounding old musician

indicators.note: surrounding means the honour goes around the abbreviation for old

parts.note: OBE, Order of the British Empire, is a British honour

explanation.surface: A veteran player receives a royal award.
explanation.walkthrough: 'musician' defines by the instrument's name for its player, as in 'second oboe'.
explanation.definitionFit: In an orchestra a woodwind player is often called by the instrument, as in first violin.

clue.text: Sneak attending class with hesitation

parts.note: in means present, as in 'in school'
a form is a school class in Britain
er is the sound of hesitating

explanation.surface: A tell-tale pupil, at school, hesitates.
explanation.walkthrough: FORM is the British school word for a class or year group.
explanation.definitionFit: A tell-tale who passes on secrets to authorities is a snitch.

clue.text: Ill-equipped female entering military group

indicators.note: entering means the female letter goes into the military group

parts.note: a unit is a body of troops

explanation.surface: A woman joins a regiment without proper gear.
explanation.definitionFit: Not suited or not competent for a task is what unsuitable means.

clue.text: Amphibian shot on river in thick mist

parts.note: a bull is a shot that hits the bull's-eye

indicators.note: in places the river inside the mist

parts.note: fog is thick mist

explanation.surface: A frog is shot beside a river in a dense fog.
explanation.definitionFit: A large frog, an amphibian with a deep bellowing croak.

clue.text: One who endures a servant like Gunga Din?

definitions.meaning: someone who puts up with, or carries, a burden
Gunga Din, in Kipling's poem, was a water-carrier for British troops in India

explanation.walkthrough: In British India a personal servant was also called by this name; Gunga Din carried water.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who tolerates hardship, and a servant who carries loads, share the same word.

clue.text: Completely safe dessert supplied to galley

parts.note: a fool is a pudding of fruit puree folded into cream
a galley proof is a printer's trial sheet, so galley stands for proof

explanation.surface: A pudding is served to a ship's kitchen with no risk at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'galley' looks like a ship's kitchen, but here it is the printing sense: a galley is a proof sheet. FOOL is a British fruit-and-cream pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: Something so well designed that nobody can get it wrong is safe beyond any doubt.

clue.text: Female evangelist's unlikely blessing

parts.note: Luke is one of the four gospel writers, the evangelists

explanation.surface: A woman gospel writer bestows a surprising benediction.
explanation.definitionFit: A lucky chance that nobody could have expected is a stroke of good fortune.

clue.text: Begin to understand, on following this thread?

definitions.text: Begin to understand, on following this thread?

parts.words: Begin to understand, on following this thread?
parts.note: the word wanted is a kind of thread, and with 'on' placed after it, it makes the idiom for starting to grasp something

explanation.surface: Someone tugs at a loose thread and slowly starts to see the point.
explanation.walkthrough: COTTON ON is British slang for coming to understand; the clue says that putting 'on' after this thread gives that phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Cotton is spun yarn used for sewing, and the phrase with on means to catch on.

clue.text: Initially panicked by snake, he goes on rabbiting

indicators.note: initially means take only the opening letter of the word panicked

parts.note: a rattler is a rattlesnake

explanation.surface: A man startled by a rattlesnake starts babbling nervously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rabbiting' is British slang (from rhyming slang 'rabbit and pork', talk) for chattering on.
explanation.definitionFit: A chatterer is someone who talks at length about trivial things.

clue.text: Demoralised soldiers retreating in stupid situation

indicators.note: in tells us the turned soldiers sit within the word for stupid

parts.note: dopy means slow-witted or stupid

indicators.note: retreating means the soldiers' letters go backwards, falling back as troops do

parts.note: OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Downhearted troops pull back from a foolish position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreating' turns the soldiers backwards to RO; 'in' sets it after the first letter of the stupid word.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone dispirited sags and droops, so low in spirits.

clue.text: It puts the edge on new tools in East

indicators.note: new signals the letters of tools and in are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A whetstone sharpens fresh tools out East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' gives OILSTON, the anagram of the two fodder words, with E after.
explanation.definitionFit: A fine-grained whetstone, lubricated with oil, sharpens blades.

clue.text: He puts things right by backing a horse

indicators.note: backing means the word for by goes into reverse

parts.note: per means by, as in per post
a clothes horse, the frame for drying laundry, is also called an airer

explanation.surface: A punter sets matters straight by betting on a racehorse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' reverses PER to REP. 'a horse' is not a racehorse but a clothes horse, which the British also call an AIRER.
explanation.definitionFit: A mender fixes broken objects, so restores them to working order.

clue.text: A priest in South, pierced by snake's longue

parts.note: Fr is short for Father, a priest's title

indicators.note: pierced by means the snake's name is driven into the letters of in and South

parts.note: taken as written
Kaa is the python in Kipling's Jungle Book

explanation.surface: A clergyman in the south has his tongue bitten by a snake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pierced by' sets KAA between the I and N. 'tongue' means language: Afrikaans is spoken in South Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: A language spoken in South Africa, descended from Dutch.

clue.text: Distant object worth very little until 1961

parts.note: far means distant
a thing is an object

explanation.surface: A remote item was nearly worthless until the early sixties.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes the coin: a quarter of an old British penny, withdrawn in 1961.
explanation.definitionFit: This old British coin, a quarter penny, was a by-word for a tiny sum and ceased to be legal tender in 1961.

clue.text: Letting in water? Extremely unusual in underground room

indicators.note: in shows those picked letters go inside the room

parts.note: a cellar is a room below ground

indicators.note: extremely means take only the letters at the two extremes of the word unusual

explanation.surface: A basement room that is leaking is quite out of the ordinary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' picks U and L, the first and last letters of 'unusual', and 'in' puts them inside CELLAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Something made of many small cells, like an open-weave fabric or a sponge, is porous and lets liquid through.

clue.text: Italian abandons expedition to obtain plant

indicators.note: abandons means the Italian letters are dropped from the word for speed

parts.note: expedition here means speed, as does celerity
IT is a common abbreviation for Italian, as in Gin and It

explanation.surface: An Italian gives up a journey to collect a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'expedition' is not a journey but speed (CELERITY); 'abandons' removes IT.
explanation.definitionFit: A vegetable with crisp stalks, a garden crop.

clue.text: Alarm given by king in battle

indicators.note: in places the king inside the battle

parts.note: a fight is a battle or combat
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A monarch on the battlefield raises the alarm.
explanation.definitionFit: Sudden fear or a scare is what alarm means here.

clue.text: Stream rushing down mountain or into river

indicators.note: into means the word or goes inside the river

parts.note: the Trent is a major river in England
taken as written

explanation.surface: A mountain stream pours into a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' sets the word after the first letter of the English river.
explanation.definitionFit: A violent, fast-flowing stream of water.

clue.text: Scholarly types retail it freely

indicators.note: freely suggests the letters of retail and it are arranged loosely into a new order

explanation.surface: Academics sell their wares without restriction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'freely' rearranges RETAIL + IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Learned, well-read people, the intellectual elite, are the educated class.

clue.text: Argumentative type who's prepared to make use of blade?

definitions.meaning: someone who rows, rhyming with cows, is a quarreller

definitions.text: who's prepared to make use of blade?
definitions.meaning: an oarsman, the blade being the flat end of an oar

explanation.definitionFit: One word for a quarreller and for an oarsman, said two ways.

clue.text: It holds meat together at a more oblique angle

definitions.meaning: a pointed rod pushed through pieces of meat for cooking
the comparative of skew, meaning more slanted

explanation.definitionFit: A kebab spike pins meat, and as a comparative adjective the word means more askew.

clue.text: Forgo flutter, say

indicators.note: say signals the word is meant as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: to wave is to flutter, as a flag does

explanation.surface: Give up a little bet, as it were.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flutter' suggests a small bet, but here it is to wave.
explanation.definitionFit: To give up a right or claim is to relinquish it.

clue.text: Legal right of fellow who's been set up

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the name is written bottom to top

parts.note: Neil is a man's name

explanation.surface: A man who was framed has a legal claim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' suggests being framed, but in a down answer it reverses NEIL.
explanation.definitionFit: A right to hold another's property until a debt is paid.

clue.text: Give fresh impetus to work initially by Descartes

parts.note: René Descartes was the French philosopher

indicators.note: initially takes just the opening letter of the word work

explanation.surface: A philosopher's early writing revitalises the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' picks W from 'work'; 'by' means beside, so RENE (Descartes's first name) is followed by W.
explanation.definitionFit: To revive or restore something is to give it new life.

clue.text: Musical boy — one rejected for following a model

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so every piece is read in reverse order

parts.note: Evita is the Lloyd Webber stage musical
Tim is a boy's name
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A young singer in a show is turned down for copying someone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' reverses the whole run EVITA + TIM + I, giving IMITATIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Copying an example or pattern is what something derivative does.

clue.text: Move fast on degree? On the contrary

definitions.text: Move fast on degree? On the contrary

parts.words: Move fast on degree? On the contrary
parts.note: the opposite of hurrying to complete a degree is dawdling over it, the idiom for moving slowly and delaying

explanation.surface: A student is urged to speed through a qualification, or rather the reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: To delay deliberately or go slowly is the opposite of hurrying.
